title: Non-blocking follow-ups from PR #108 review (frontend-oscillator-chart)
description: Non-blocking findings from pr-reviewer's review of PR #108 (frontend-oscillator-chart), recorded here so they aren't lost once that PR merges. The blocking finding -- OscillatorChart.tsx crashing the whole app when a plotted point has a null stochastic_k/force_index_2ema (e.g. selecting the 'Max' range, which includes the indicator warm-up bars) -- is tracked as the needs_work verdict on the parent task itself, not here.

checklist.step: backend: GET /api/stocks/{ticker}/indicators' IndicatorHistoryPoint.stochastic_k/force_index_2ema are declared `type: number` (required, non-nullable) in backend/app/api/schemas.py and backend/openapi.json, but the runtime response can legitimately emit `null` for early-history bars still inside the indicator's warm-up window (Stochastic %K(5,3,3) needs ~11 bars, confirmed live: GET /api/stocks/AAPL/indicators?range=max returns 6 points with stochastic_k=null and 1 with force_index_2ema=null). This is a distinct cause from the one api-stocks-analysis-nullable-indicators already fixed for /analysis (that fix drops malformed-OHLC bars; these nulls come from legitimate warm-up insufficiency on otherwise well-formed bars, so the same fix doesn't apply). Decide and implement: either mark these fields Optional/nullable in schemas.py (regenerating openapi.json + frontend types) so the contract is honest, or trim not-yet-warmed-up points from the response before it's returned.

OscillatorChart.tsx's Force Index and MACD Histogram pane setup (the HistogramSeries creation, sign-based color computation, and dotted zero-baseline price line) is near-duplicated between the two panes with only the series title/paneIndex differing -- could be factored into one small shared helper to reduce the ~20 lines of duplication, mirroring the 'single buildOscillatorSeriesData pass' consolidation already done for the data-building side.

OscillatorChart.tsx's createChart() call (line ~135) uses the exact same options object (`{ autoSize: true, layout: { background: { color: 'transparent' } } }`) as PriceChart.tsx's own chart-creation effect, duplicated verbatim in a second file -- a shared helper (e.g. a small `createBaseChart(container)` in a features/stocks lib module) would remove the duplication and the risk of the two drifting apart if the base chart options ever need to change. (Surfaced by a code-review skill pass on this PR.)

Non-blocking (round-2 re-review, PR #108): the new `createBaseChart` helper landed at `frontend/src/features/stocks/lib/chart.ts`, but per docs/architecture/Frontend.md §3's explicit utils/-vs-features placement test ('domain-agnostic (doesn't reference a feature's domain concepts) and not a component -> utils/'), it arguably belongs in `frontend/src/utils/` instead -- it takes only a raw `HTMLElement` and returns a generic `IChartApi`, with no reference to ticker/position/signal or any stocks-domain concept, the same test that puts `utils/format.ts` outside any single feature folder. Frontend.md's own documented directory tree also only lists `hooks/` and `components/` under each `features/<domain>/` folder, not a `lib/` subfolder, so this is a new, undocumented structural pattern as well as an arguable placement call. Genuinely arguable rather than clear-cut though: its only two consumers (PriceChart.tsx, OscillatorChart.tsx) are both in features/stocks today, unlike format.ts's cross-feature usage that motivated the utils/ example -- worth a decision either way (move to utils/, or document the features/<domain>/lib/ pattern in Frontend.md as an accepted convention) rather than leaving it unresolved.

decisions.decision: Addressed the two frontend-only follow-ups (near-duplicated Force Index/MACD Histogram pane setup, and the duplicated createChart() options object) as part of the frontend-oscillator-chart PR #108 needs_work fix round, since both were small and directly touched the same file already being fixed for the blocking bug. Added `addZeroBaselineHistogramPane` (a shared helper in OscillatorChart.tsx) for the first, and a new `features/stocks/lib/chart.ts` with `createBaseChart(container)` (used by both PriceChart.tsx and OscillatorChart.tsx) for the second. Left the first checklist item (backend schemas.py nullable-fields decision) untouched -- that's genuinely backend-area work outside a frontend PR's natural scope, and this fix round's frontend null-guard already makes the crash-safety fix independent of which backend approach is eventually chosen there.
decisions.rationale: Both fixes verified via the same test run as the parent task's blocking fix: vitest (259 passed, coverage unaffected), eslint, tsc -b --noEmit, and make e2e (13/13 passed) -- see frontend-oscillator-chart's own decisions entry for full detail. Not marking this whole task's `state` as `done` since checklist item 1 (backend) remains open and is out of scope for a frontend change.

decisions.decision: Marked IndicatorHistoryPoint.stochastic_k/force_index_2ema Optional (`float | None = Field(default=None, ...)`) in backend/app/api/schemas.py, rather than trimming not-yet-warmed-up points out of the response. Regenerated backend/openapi.json (python scripts/export_openapi.py) and frontend/src/api/types.ts (npm run generate:api-types) from it.
decisions.rationale: Trimming was rejected: a bar within Stochastic's ~11-bar or Force Index's ~2-bar warm-up window still has perfectly valid ema_13/ema_26/macd_histogram/bull_power/bear_power/signal/confidence values (confirmed by tracing app/indicators/stochastic.py and app/indicators/force_index.py -- pandas ewm-based indicators never produce NaN even on the very first bar, only the rolling-window-based Stochastic and the diff-seeded Force Index do, and only for their own first few bars respectively), and PriceChart.tsx's EMA/signal overlay is fed from this same endpoint's same points -- trimming the whole point would silently drop valid EMA/signal data for those early bars too, degrading the price-chart overlay to fix an oscillator-pane-only problem. Nullable-schema keeps every point present with only the two genuinely-undefined fields marked as such, matching how OscillatorChart.tsx's buildOscillatorSeriesData already filters each of its three series independently (a null stochastic_k on a bar doesn't suppress that same bar's valid force_index_2ema). This is a different situation from api-stocks-analysis-nullable-indicators' NaN-from-malformed-OHLC fix (which correctly chose to drop the bad bar instead of widening the schema) -- that NaN represented actually-corrupt input data cascading into a wrong trigger/wave computation, a correctness bug; this null represents a structurally well-formed bar that simply doesn't have enough trailing history yet for one specific rolling-window indicator, which is expected and bounded (always exactly the first few bars of whatever range was requested) rather than a data-quality problem. Verified the new nullable behavior with a new backend test (test_early_bars_have_null_stochastic_k_and_force_index in tests/integration/test_stocks_indicator_history.py) asserting the exact warm-up bar counts (6 for stochastic_k, 1 for force_index_2ema) traced from each indicator's own docstring, and confirmed every other field stays non-null across the same warm-up window. Also updated OscillatorChart.tsx's isFiniteValue doc comment to note the type/reality mismatch it originally worked around is now fixed, while keeping the runtime guard itself (an honestly-nullable-typed value is exactly as unplottable to Lightweight Charts as a dishonestly-typed one that happens to be null) -- the guard's `unknown` parameter type is intentionally kept rather than narrowed to the new `number | null | undefined` generated type, so it keeps working unconditionally regardless of a caller's declared type, consistent with PriceChart.tsx's analogous hasFiniteOhlc guard.

decisions.decision: Moved createBaseChart from frontend/src/features/stocks/lib/chart.ts to frontend/src/utils/chart.ts, updating both PriceChart.tsx's and OscillatorChart.tsx's imports. Did not introduce a features/<domain>/lib/ convention.
decisions.rationale: Applied Frontend.md §3's utils/-vs-features placement test literally: createBaseChart takes a raw HTMLElement and returns a generic IChartApi, referencing no stocks-domain concept (ticker/position/signal) at all -- exactly the 'domain-agnostic and not a component -> utils/' case the doc spells out, and the same test (not merely the same outcome) that already places utils/format.ts outside any single feature folder despite format.ts also having started from feature-specific consumers. Rejected the alternative (documenting a new features/<domain>/lib/ convention in Frontend.md instead): Frontend.md §3's directory tree is explicit that a features/<domain>/ folder owns only hooks/ and components/, and introducing a third subfolder kind for exactly one two-line helper is more structural surface than the problem needs when an existing, already-documented location (utils/) fits it exactly. The 'both consumers are in features/stocks today' argument the follow-up task raised as a countervailing point doesn't actually distinguish this from format.ts's history (format.ts's own initial consumer set was similarly narrow before a second feature adopted it) and the placement test itself is about what the helper *is* (domain-agnostic, no props/rendering), not how many current call sites happen to share a folder.
